column1: # boru Language Specification: error-taxonomy edge cases II
# Continuation of edge-errors-1.tsv: the catch-and-substitute idiom
# through fn boundaries, raising out of control contexts (if / case /
# fold / filter), reserved words, parse-time numeric taxonomy, the §5
# uncalled_function residue check, and structural assertions.
# §1  the catch-and-substitute idiom — errors stay local to a boundary
def sd fn [[a:Integer b:Integer] [Integer] [do [a div b] error [drop -1]]] sd 10 2
column3: a fn wraps a risky op: the success path is untouched

column1: def sd fn [[a:Integer b:Integer] [Integer] [do [a div b] error [drop -1]]] sd 10 0
column3: …and the failure path substitutes the sentinel INSIDE the fn

column1: def mk fn [[] [Error] [do [raise mk_c "m"]]] (mk) dot code eq mk_c/q
column3: a fn may DECLARE an Error return and hand the reified value out
an Error value renders as error(message) inside a container

column1: def e (do [raise aa "x"]) def m {e: e} m.e is Error
column3: a map field holds an Error like any value
two independently reified errors coexist as data
convert Map projects code, message, AND the payload key

column1: (convert Map (do [raise {code: cc/q, message: "m", n: 7}])) get "n" eq 7
column3: …and the payload value survives the projection

column1: do [convert Integer "abc"] error [dot message] eq 'convert: cannot convert "abc" to number'
column3: a plain Go-error's message is still readable at the boundary

column1: # §2  raising out of control contexts — one boundary catches them all
do [if true [raise t_c "t"] [5]] error [dot code] eq t_c/q
column3: raise from an if branch

column1: do [1 case [1 [raise one_c "u"] 2]] error [dot code] eq one_c/q
column3: raise from a case arm

column1: do [[1 2] filter [raise fi_c "f"]] error [dot code] eq fi_c/q
column3: raise from a filter predicate aborts the filter

column1: # §3  reserved words and parse-time numeric taxonomy

column3: the boolean literals cannot be rebound
the sealed core words cannot be rebound
…nor undef'd

column2: ERROR:does not unify with declared type
column3: a typed def rejects a non-conforming value loudly
an integer LITERAL past MaxInt is rejected at parse
…however it is spelled
a negative overflowing float literal is rejected at parse too
a negative strict index misses loudly
a wrapper call matching no signature leaves the fn as data — the end-of-run drain names it
…same through any module wrapper
Assert.equal compares lists structurally
…and maps
a one-field difference fails
Assert.throws accepts a user raise, not just native errors

column1: import "boru:test" Test.test "a" [Assert.ok none] end Test.test "b" [Assert.ok none] end Test.fail-count
column3: failures accumulate across recorded tests

column1: import "boru:test" Test.test "f" [Assert.ok none] end Test.test "p" [Assert.ok 1] end Test.summary
column3: a failing test never stops a later passing one

column1: # §6  the parse nesting guard — a deterministic evaluation_limit
# (maxParseNestingDepth is a parser constant, so this is not budget-dependent)

column3: source nested past the parser depth limit fails loudly at parse, never a stack overflow

column1: # §7  boundary discipline — what the error branch leaves behind
do [raise a1 "1" raise a2 "2"] error [dot code] eq a1/q
column3: the FIRST raise aborts the body; a later raise never runs
a none success value passes through like any value
nested successful boundaries collapse transparently
a handler may resolve to none — that is its result
the routed code is a first-class Atom
the routed message is the raise's short detail

column1: do [raise {code: lim/q, message: "m", max: 10}] error [dot max] eq 10
column3: a handler can route on payload alone

column1: do [raise {code: lim/q, message: "m", max: 10}] error [case [[dot code eq lim/q] [dot max] 0]] eq 10
column3: predicate case arms inspect the Error; the block reads its payload
NUR031: an Error is a value-like Ideal — eq compares its fields (equal code + message), like two equal scalars
…and differing codes make them unequal

column1: def e (do [raise aa "x"]) (e dot code eq aa/q) and (e dot message eq "x")
column3: a bound Error value reads repeatedly without being consumed
the empty string is truthy — only none and false are falsy
Assert.equal compares across the numeric tower
two nones are equal — not-equal fails
a success value is not an Error — is stays a clean discriminator
a Boolean success value passes through the no-op branch

column1: def h fn [[e:Error] [Atom] [e dot code]] h (do [raise hh_c "m"]) eq hh_c/q
column3: Error is a first-class param type — handlers can be ordinary fns

column1: def e (do [raise aa "x"]) e dot got eq none
column3: a missing payload key reads as none, mirroring map reads

column1: do [raise {code: z9/q, message: ""}] error [dot message] size
column3: an EMPTY message is legal in the map form

column1: do [raise {message: "m", code: ok2/q}] error [dot code] eq ok2/q
column3: spec-map key order is irrelevant
subtracting a negative overflows at the top like adding
landing EXACTLY on MinInt by multiplication is fine
